Convert a preference fit to a matrix of saved posterior draws

Source: R/mcmc_interoperability.R
mcmc_interoperability.Rd

Columns q[i] are item strengths divided by their sum in each saved draw. With normalise = FALSE, theta[i] are the stored, unnormalised strengths. The index i follows fit$data$item_labels. K_item and K_ranking contain occupied-group counts when available. Only retained draws are returned.

All fits must use identical data (including item order) and model specification, and have the same number of retained draws. The caller must supply independently run chains, preferably with different seeds and initialisations; these converters cannot establish independence.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'btsbm_fit'
as.matrix(x, ..., normalise = TRUE, pars = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'btsbm_fit'
as.array(x, ..., normalise = TRUE, pars = NULL)

as_draws_array(x, normalise = TRUE, pars = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'btsbm_fit'
as.mcmc(x, ..., normalise = TRUE, pars = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'btsbm_fit'
as.mcmc.list(x, ..., normalise = TRUE, pars = NULL)

as_mcmc_chains(x, normalise = TRUE, pars = NULL)

Arguments

x

One btsbm_fit, or a non-empty list of fits from independent runs.

...

Reserved for generic compatibility.

normalise

Logical; report sum-to-one item strengths by default.

pars

Optional parameter names, as in as.matrix.btsbm_fit().

Value

A numeric matrix with saved draws in rows and quantities in columns.

An array with dimensions iteration, chain, parameter. A single fit contains one chain. Warm-up is already excluded.

as_draws_array returns an iteration by chain by parameter array. as_mcmc_chains returns a coda mcmc.list, retaining original iteration numbering. Its chains must also have equal warm-up lengths.

A coda mcmc object. Its first iteration is warmup + 1 and thin is 1.

Details

Variable-length block-strength vectors and arbitrary allocation labels are deliberately excluded. Mixture and LBM fits currently expose group counts only, because a single profile-independent item-strength vector is absent. For coda::gelman.diag(), use multivariate = FALSE: sum-to-one strengths have a singular joint covariance. A constant group-count trace can also have undefined convergence diagnostics. coda and bayesplot are optional.
